title: Understanding Financial Services for Investigators
summary: A foundation eight-module programme explaining how financial services firms work, what records they hold, and how investigators can request and read them.
intro: This training programme equips investigators and analysts to understand how banks, payment firms, investment firms, funds, trust and company service providers and crypto-asset service providers work, what records they hold, and how to request and read them.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give investigators and analysts a clear, practical understanding of the financial services firms they meet in their cases and the information those firms hold. Participants leave able to identify where relevant records are likely to sit, frame precise requests, read the material that comes back and spot what is missing.
sections.What It Covers: How the financial system fits together, banks and correspondent banking, payment and e-money firms, investment firms, brokers and funds, trust and company service providers, crypto-asset service providers, firms' due diligence, record-keeping and reporting obligations, and making and reading requests for records.
Intended Audience: Police and agency investigators new to financial investigation
FIU, intelligence and asset recovery staff who request or analyse financial records
Customs, tax and other enforcement officers who need a working knowledge of financial services firms
Learning Objectives: Explain how the main types of financial services firm operate and connect
Identify the records each type of firm is likely to hold
Describe firms' customer due diligence, record-keeping and reporting obligations
Frame precise, lawful requests for financial information
Read and interpret statements, payment messages and onboarding files
Recognise gaps, inconsistencies and red flags in financial records
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a plain-language briefing with sample records and request-drafting exercises, ending in a records workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the sectors most relevant to participants' cases.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior knowledge of financial services is required. Some experience of investigation or intelligence work is helpful.
Core Reading: FATF (2012, as updated), International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations
FATF (2012), Operational Issues: Financial Investigations Guidance
FATF (2016), Guidance on Correspondent Banking Services
FATF (2021), Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers

modules.title: The Financial System for Investigators
modules.summary: An introduction to how money moves through the financial system, the main types of firm and how they are regulated, and why understanding them makes investigators more effective.
objectives: Describe the main sectors and types of financial services firm
Explain how payment, clearing and settlement systems connect firms
Outline how firms are licensed and supervised
syllabus: The main sectors: banking, payments, investment, funds and fiduciary services
How money moves: payment systems, clearing and settlement
Licensing, supervision and the role of the supervisor
Why knowing the firm matters to an investigation

modules.title: Banks and Correspondent Banking
modules.summary: How retail, private and corporate banks operate, how correspondent relationships move money across borders, and what account, payment and customer records banks hold.
objectives: Explain retail, private and corporate banking products
Describe correspondent banking and cross-border payment chains
Identify the records banks hold and where they sit
syllabus: Current, savings, loan and trade finance products
Private banking and wealth management
Correspondent banking, nested relationships and payment messages
Bank records: onboarding files, statements, payment data and alerts

modules.title: Payment and E-Money Firms
modules.summary: How payment institutions, e-money issuers, money remitters and card schemes work, how they differ from banks, and the transaction and device data they hold.
objectives: Explain the business models of payment, e-money and remittance firms
Describe the roles of card issuers, acquirers, schemes and payment processors
Identify the transaction, account and device data these firms hold
syllabus: Payment institutions, e-money issuers and money remitters
Cards: issuers, acquirers, schemes and merchants
Agents, distributors and safeguarded customer funds
Records: transaction logs, IP and device data and merchant files

modules.title: Investment Firms, Brokers and Funds
modules.summary: How investment firms, brokers, custodians and investment funds hold and move client assets, and the account, trading and investor records they maintain.
objectives: Explain the roles of brokers, wealth managers, custodians and fund administrators
Describe how funds are structured and how investors subscribe and redeem
Identify trading, custody and investor records relevant to investigations
syllabus: Brokers, wealth managers and portfolio managers
Custody, nominee accounts and omnibus structures
Funds, managers, administrators and transfer agents
Records: client files, trade data, custody statements and investor registers

modules.title: Trust and Company Service Providers
modules.summary: What trust and company service providers do, how they form and administer companies, trusts and foundations, and the ownership and control information they hold.
objectives: Explain the services trust and company service providers offer
Describe how companies, trusts and foundations are formed and administered
Identify beneficial ownership and control records held by providers
syllabus: Company formation, registered office and nominee services
Trusts and foundations: trustees, settlors, protectors and beneficiaries
Beneficial ownership information and registers
Records: due diligence files, minutes, ledgers and bank mandates

modules.title: Crypto-Asset Service Providers
modules.summary: How crypto-asset exchanges, custodians and brokers operate, how they connect to the traditional financial system, and the customer and transaction records they hold.
objectives: Explain the main crypto-asset service provider business models
Describe how fiat on-ramps and off-ramps connect to banks and payment firms
Identify customer, wallet and travel rule records held by providers
syllabus: Exchanges, custodial wallet providers, brokers and kiosks
Fiat on-ramps and off-ramps and banking relationships
Customer files, wallet addresses and blockchain transaction data
Travel rule information and requests across providers

modules.title: What Firms Must Keep: Due Diligence, Records and Reports
modules.summary: The AML/CFT obligations that shape what firms know about their customers, how long records are kept, and how internal alerts and suspicious transaction reports are produced.
objectives: Explain customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence obligations
Describe record-keeping requirements and retention periods
Understand how monitoring alerts and suspicious transaction reports are generated
syllabus: Customer due diligence, beneficial ownership and enhanced checks
Record-keeping: what must be kept and for how long
Transaction monitoring, alerts and internal investigations
Suspicious transaction reporting and tipping-off constraints

modules.title: Requesting and Reading Records: Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a practical exercise in which participants frame requests to different firms, read the records produced and identify gaps and lines of enquiry.
objectives: Draft precise, proportionate requests for financial records
Read statements, payment messages and onboarding files accurately
Identify gaps, inconsistencies and follow-up enquiries
syllabus: Choosing the right firm, power and point of contact
Drafting requests: scope, period, format and confidentiality
Reading sample records from banks, payment and crypto-asset firms
Workshop: from records to lines of enquiry

related.title: Asset Recovery: Tracing, Freezing and Confiscation
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping practitioners to trace, restrain, confiscate, manage and return criminal assets, including crypto-assets and assets held abroad.

related.title: Financial Investigation: Following the Money
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping investigators and analysts to run parallel financial investigations, trace funds through accounts and corporate vehicles, and present financial evidence.

related.title: FIU Operational and Strategic Analysis
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping FIU analysts to prioritise and analyse reports, produce operational and strategic intelligence, and cooperate effectively at home and abroad.

related.title: Fraud and Cyber-Enabled Financial Crime Investigations
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping investigators and FIU analysts to tackle fraud, money mules and ransomware proceeds, working with banks and payment firms to recover funds.

related.title: Prosecuting Financial Crime: Evidence, Experts and the Courtroom
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping prosecutors and judges to handle money laundering and complex financial crime cases, from charge and evidence to sentencing and confiscation.

related.title: Public-Private Partnerships and Financial Intelligence Sharing
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping FIUs and law-enforcement agencies to design, run and evaluate public-private partnerships for sharing financial intelligence lawfully and effectively.
